_note: Sound bank of The Motel (S8, 2026-11-16). Format as in games/motel/sfx-events.json: events[name] = {files (random pick), kids (softer set for kids mode), gain, pitch [min, max] playback rate, cooldown s, loop}. Paths are relative to this file. Extra fields are advice for the player code: space = where it should sound ('3d' = at the thing, through the panner; '2d' = in the head), note, added = an event that sfx-events.json does not have yet (S4 wires it when the feature exists), text/seconds for voice lines. All files are OGG Vorbis 44.1 kHz; one-shots mono, beds and stingers stereo (play stereo files 2D only). Every file is a cut of a downloaded recording (SOURCES.tsv); nothing is synthesized. Chosen by name and measurement, not by ear: each family needs one listening pass.
_levels: One-shots peak at -1 to -6 dBFS; gun families are levelled to one RMS each (pistol -19 ... shotgun -15), so 'gain' is the mix: guns 0.85-1.0, impacts 0.7-0.85, zombies 0.8-1.0 (3D distance does the rest), music 0.3-0.45, ambience 0.5-0.6, voice 1.0 (duck music by 6 dB under a line).
_music: music.calm/wave/intense/boss are beds cut from Sonniss trailer and horror libraries (no credit needed). music.wave and music.intense have the same length and pulse, so they crossfade without a bump. The *.ccby events are full music alternatives by Kevin MacLeod (CC BY 4.0): they may be used only together with the credit lines in vr-arena/_sound-src/LICENSES.md on a credits screen of the product.
_memory: The player code decodes every file under 'events' at load: about 150 MB of decoded audio at 48 kHz. Beds (music.*, ambience.*, world.heli.*) are the big ones; decode them on first use or play them through an <audio> element if memory is tight on Quest 2. 'alternatives' is NOT loaded: copy an entry into 'events' to use it.

shot.shotgun.note: blast only; play shotgun.pump 0.35 s later

gun.reload.note: magazine out at 0 s, in at 0.9 s (about 1.4 s)

gun.mag.out.added: the two halves of gun.reload on their own, for reloads of another length

shotgun.pump.added: pump after every shotgun blast (0.35 s later)

shell.drop.added: a spent case landing, 0.35-0.5 s after a shot

bullet.impact.metal.added: a missed bullet hitting a prop / the ground

bullet.impact.wood.added: a missed bullet hitting a prop / the ground

melee.swing.added: axe / machete swing through the air (tip speed over 2.2 m/s)

melee.saw.idle.note: 1.85 s seamless slice: play as a loop while held

melee.saw.start.added: the chainsaw is taken / the trigger is first pulled

zombie.death.note: kids: only the soft body fall

zombie.bodyfall.added: the body reaching the ground, 0.4-0.6 s after zombie.death

fence.rattle.added: leapers shake the fence 2 s before the first one jumps

boss.windup.added: rising whoosh while the thrown thing is in the air (about 1.2 s before boss.slam)

boss.slam.added: the thrown wreck / the ground smash landing

stinger.wave.added: a hit under the WAVE n title

stinger.boss.added: when the boss is first seen

stinger.jump.added: first digger, a leaper landing behind a player; never in kids mode

riser.10s.added: last 10 s of the prep and of each break; ends on the wave start

score.tick.added: score counting up on the end screen (raise the pitch as it climbs)

plank.drop.added: a torn plank landing inside the zone

chest.open.note: latch, hinge creak, lid slam at 1.05 s

world.neon.hum.added: loop: the sign buzzing; stop it in the blackout

world.spark.added: the sign flickering (boss steps, power failing)

world.alarm.note: 4 s seamless alarm figure: repeat it while the alarm lasts

world.heli.away.added: 16 s: the helicopter leaving at the start of the prep (take-off part of the recording)

world.heli.in.added: 12 s: rotor growing for the pick-up at the win (rotor at speed, long fade-in)

radio.open.added: walkie-talkie squelch around a voice.radio.* line

radio.close.added: walkie-talkie squelch around a voice.radio.* line

ambience.night.note: crickets + wind in trees, 30 s seamless

ambience.rain.added: loop for the storm of the last wave

music.wave.note: the library's own seamless pulse loop

music.intense.note: music.wave with two more layers on top, same length: crossfades cleanly from music.wave

music.boss.note: the pulse of music.wave under a darker cinematic layer, same length

voice.tent_pick.text: Pick who you want to be. Grab a figure off the table.

voice.tent_brief.text: The motel is overrun. Hold the car park until I get back.

voice.tent_go.text: Wheels up. Good luck down there.

voice.prep_weapons.text: Weapons are on the ground. Squeeze the grip to pick one up.

voice.prep_gates.text: Grab a hammer and board up those gates.

voice.wave_2.text: Wave two. They are getting faster.

voice.wave_clear_b.text: That is all of them. Breathe.

voice.wave_clear_c.text: Clear. Reload and patch the gates.

voice.supply_in.text: Supply drop coming in. Heads up!

voice.supply_down.text: Crate is down. Grab the new guns.

voice.jumpers.text: Jumpers! They are coming over the fence!

voice.spitter.text: Spitter! Stay out of the green!

voice.archer.text: Archer on the roof! Keep moving!

voice.paratroopers.text: Dead paratroopers! Shoot them out of the sky!

voice.bloater.text: Do not let that one get close!

voice.blackout_2.text: Stay close. Watch each other's backs.

voice.boss_seen.text: That is the big one. Aim for the head!

voice.boss_dead.text: He is down! He is down!

voice.down.text: Man down! Get to your teammate!

voice.last.text: You are the last one standing!

voice.wipe.text: Get up. We are not done.

voice.win_3.text: Mission complete. Drinks are on me.

voice.lose_1.text: I have lost them. Returning to base.

voice.lose_2.text: You held as long as you could.

music.boss.ccby.added: alternative bed: "Killers" by Kevin MacLeod, CC BY 4.0, credit required; to use it, put this file first in music.boss
